passages.text: GRANITE, a hard stone composed of grains of quartz, felspar, and mica, closely joined together without any cement.
Mr Werner and his followers hold that granite is the oldest of all rocks, the first that was deposited from the waters of the universal ocean which once covered the whole globe.
Being formed before plants and animals existed, it contains no remains of them, and is therefore called a primitive rock.
Dr Hutton, on the contrary, maintains that granite was once melted by subterraneous heat and forced up among the other strata; but this opinion has fewer followers.
Granite forms the nucleus and the highest summits of all great mountain chains.
It is every where the lowest rock, upon which all others rest.
Granite is a coarse-grained igneous rock composed mostly of quartz, alkali feldspar and plagioclase, usually with mica or amphibole.
Granite forms from magma that cools and crystallises slowly deep underground. It is an intrusive igneous rock, not a sedimentary rock laid down in water.

In the late 18th century, Abraham Gottlob Werner's Neptunist school held that granite had settled out of a primeval ocean. James Hutton argued instead that it had once been molten, and his view prevailed in the 19th century.
Granite contains no fossils because it crystallised from molten rock.
Granite intrusions often cut across the rocks around them, which shows that the granite is younger than those rocks.
Large granite bodies are common in the cores of mountain ranges, where uplift and erosion have exposed them.
Granites of many different ages exist, from billions of years old to only a few million years old.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: quartz, feldspar, mica, Werner, Hutton.
Neptunism scores well on the theory but leaves out the rock itself.

alignments.label: What granite is made of

britannica.quote: grains of quartz, felspar, and mica

wikipedia.quote: composed mostly of quartz, alkali feldspar and plagioclase, usually with mica

alignments.note: Same minerals. Felspar is now spelt feldspar and split into two kinds.

alignments.label: Settled from an ocean

britannica.quote: deposited from the waters of the universal ocean which once covered the whole globe

wikipedia.quote: not a sedimentary rock laid down in water

alignments.note: Werner's Neptunism. Granite crystallises from molten rock, and no world ocean ever covered the globe.

alignments.label: The oldest rock

britannica.quote: granite is the oldest of all rocks

wikipedia.quote: Granites of many different ages exist

alignments.note: Some granites are among the youngest rocks in their region.

alignments.label: No fossils

britannica.quote: Being formed before plants and animals existed, it contains no remains of them

wikipedia.quote: Granite contains no fossils because it crystallised from molten rock

alignments.note: Right that it has no fossils, wrong about why: molten rock destroys them, whatever its age.

alignments.label: Hutton's molten granite

britannica.quote: granite was once melted by subterraneous heat and forced up among the other strata

wikipedia.quote: James Hutton argued instead that it had once been molten

alignments.note: The minority view of 1810 is the accepted view today.

alignments.label: Fewer followers

wikipedia.quote: his view prevailed in the 19th century

alignments.note: True in 1810, no longer: Hutton's side won within a few decades.

alignments.label: Mountain summits

britannica.quote: forms the nucleus and the highest summits of all great mountain chains

wikipedia.quote: common in the cores of mountain ranges

alignments.note: Common in mountain cores, yes. In all great chains and at the highest summits, no.

alignments.label: The lowest rock

britannica.quote: It is every where the lowest rock, upon which all others rest

wikipedia.quote: Granite intrusions often cut across the rocks around them

alignments.note: Granite often pushes up into rocks laid down before it, so it is not always at the bottom.

suggestedQuestions: Who was right about granite in 1810, Werner or Hutton?
Why does granite contain no fossils?
Is granite always the oldest and lowest rock?

Who was right about granite in 1810, Wer.answer: Hutton. In 1810 most followed Werner, who held that granite settled out of a universal ocean [B2]; Hutton's view that it had been molten had fewer followers [B4]. Wikipedia says granite forms from magma that cools slowly underground [W2], and that Hutton's view prevailed in the 19th century [W3].

Why does granite contain no fossils?.answer: The 1810 entry says granite formed before plants and animals existed [B3]. Wikipedia says the reason is that it crystallised from molten rock [W4]. Both agree there are no fossils; they disagree about why.

Is granite always the oldest and lowest.answer: No. The 1810 entry calls it the oldest of all rocks [B2] and the lowest everywhere [B6]. Wikipedia says granites of many ages exist [W7], and that granite intrusions often cut across older rocks around them [W5].
